description: Run ONE read-only SQL statement against the configured Snowflake account. Read leaders only (SELECT/SHOW/DESCRIBE/EXPLAIN/WITH). Returns immediately with a job_id and status 'queued' (D0.3 deferred-completion shape) -- the dispatch returning is NOT the same as the job finishing. The result is ALWAYS written to the caller-supplied output_tsv_path, never returned inline, at any size. Snowflake's own Python connector documentation imposes no vendor row ceiling on a query result -- arraysize and client_prefetch_threads are client-side performance knobs, not caps; fetchall() retrieves all remaining rows with no stated maximum -- so the limit below is entirely our own policy. Defaults to 500 rows to avoid exhausting warehouse compute and disk, and to discourage pulling all rows for client-side filtering that a WHERE clause should do instead. To fetch more, pass acknowledge_default_limit_override=true together with an explicit row_limit (up to 1000) -- both are required together, and a row_limit above 1000 is refused rather than silently clamped. For pulls beyond 1000 rows, use export_query instead (same override mechanism, hard cap 50000). When the goal is validating that records exist or picking one to act on next, prefer selecting stable ID columns over email addresses or other PII-bearing fields -- the query decides what columns come back, so a narrower SELECT is both cheaper and lower-exposure.
embedding_description: Run an ad-hoc read-only SQL query against the operator's Snowflake data warehouse and land the columns and rows in a workspace TSV file -- never inline, at any size. Dispatches asynchronously, returning a job_id while the query runs in the background. Defaults to 500 rows unless acknowledged otherwise. The everyday query surface over the warehouse.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dispatch envelope: job_id (string) and status ('queued'). This is NOT the query result -- that arrives separately when the job completes and is delivered as its own message: path (the written .tsv file in the operator's workspace), columns (ordered names), row_count, and truncated (true when row_count hit the effective limit -- more rows may exist).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This call only confirms the job was queued -- do not present job_id/status as the query result. Acknowledge the request is in flight; the TSV handle itself lands in a follow-up message when the job completes. Once delivered: confirm the path, the row_count, and the column list. The file may contain potentially sensitive corporate warehouse content (data_sensitivity 0.5) -- name the path for downstream use but never inline its contents into context. If truncated is true, say so and point to export_query or an acknowledged row_limit override for the rest.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Run a read-only SQL query against the configured Snowflake account and write the result to a workspace TSV file.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: snowflake.invalid_params: missing sql/output_tsv_path, the path's parent directory does not exist, acknowledge_default_limit_override and row_limit were not given together, or row_limit exceeded the 1000 hard cap. snowflake.export_path_refused: output_tsv_path is not absolute, not a .tsv, or not contained under any operator-configured export_allowed_roots entry (an empty export_allowed_roots refuses every write by default). snowflake.read_only_violation: the statement is not a permitted read leader. snowflake.auth_failed: the key-pair JWT was rejected. snowflake.permission_denied: the role lacks privileges. snowflake.warehouse_suspended: the configured warehouse is suspended. snowflake.timeout: the query exceeded the statement timeout. snowflake.api_error: a query-syntax or other warehouse error.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: snowflake.invalid_params naming the override pair: pass BOTH acknowledge_default_limit_override=true and an explicit row_limit, or neither (for the 500-row default); a row_limit above 1000 must go through export_query instead. snowflake.invalid_params with a missing-parent message: create the parent directory first. snowflake.export_path_refused: pass an ABSOLUTE path ending in .tsv under a configured workspace root; if export_allowed_roots is empty, add the operator's export directory to the snowflake_plugin config. snowflake.read_only_violation: submit a single SELECT/SHOW/DESCRIBE/EXPLAIN/WITH statement. snowflake.warehouse_suspended: ask the operator to resume the warehouse. snowflake.timeout: narrow the query or add a LIMIT. snowflake.auth_failed/permission_denied: ask the operator to check the connecting user's key and role grants.
